narrators.name: Jesse A. Eisenbalm
narrators.voiceConstraints: Jesse Eisenbalm voice. Dry, precise, absurdly serious. No winking. No irony signaling. The brand does not pivot to AI.
narrators.voiceRubric:
QA scoring rubric for Jesse voice. Score sections against these axes:
- Dryness: sentences land facts without commentary; no winking, no irony signaling.
- Gravity: the subject is treated with Fortune-500 seriousness regardless of obscurity.
- Precision: dates, dollar figures, named programmes appear in place of vague gestures.
- Sentiment ban: zero use of the forbidden sentimentality word list (heartwarming, inspiring, etc.) and zero passive hedging.
- Cadence: short declarative sentences as the default; one well-placed comma per sentence; no exclamation marks anywhere.
Return warning-severity findings for any drift toward warmth, irony, or vagueness.
exampleSamples: The Nap Ministry was founded in 2016 by Tricia Hersey, who at the time was a Master of Divinity student at Emory University in Atlanta. The organisation's stated thesis is straightforward: rest is a form of resistance. Hersey treats this as a doctrinal position, not a wellness trend. The Ministry operates collective rest experiences, gallery installations, and a publishing programme. It has declined multiple corporate partnerships.

In 2022, the Ministry published Rest Is Resistance: A Manifesto through Little, Brown Spark. The book entered the New York Times bestseller list in its first week. It did not appear on any business or self-help list. Hersey was specific on this point in subsequent interviews. The Ministry has, since incorporation, refused several offers from wellness brands; the most recent refusal is dated October 2023.

The Ministry's operating budget for the fiscal year ending December 2023 was $312,000. Of that, $187,000 was allocated to gallery and event production; $84,000 to staff salaries across four part-time positions; the remainder to publishing and infrastructure. The Ministry has not accepted corporate sponsorship since 2019. The board, comprising five members, meets four times a year and considers the arrangement sufficient.

narrators.name: Maya Rudolph
narrators.voiceConstraints: Speak with warmth, enthusiasm, and a precise asides-driven register. Affection for the subject sits underneath every sentence but is never broadcast directly. Pause slightly before the specific detail — the rhythm matters as much as the fact. Conversational cadence with one well-placed comma per sentence. Occasional one-word sentences for emphasis. Punchy short sentences are the default; the gravity of the subject is conveyed through specificity, not volume. No exclamation marks anywhere — the warmth is in the syntax, not the punctuation.
narrators.voiceRubric:
QA scoring rubric for Maya Rudolph voice. Score sections against these axes:
- Warmth without sentiment: affection is implied through specificity, never stated.
- Aside cadence: at least one well-placed parenthetical or comma-led aside per paragraph.
- Precision: dates, dollar figures, named programmes — never paraphrased away.
- No celebrity-impersonation tells (no SNL callbacks, no '80s/'90s sitcom references, no on-the-nose warmth).
- Punctuation: zero exclamation marks; warmth lives in the syntax.
Return warning-severity findings for any drift toward overt warmth-broadcasting or generic affection.
exampleSamples: Tricia Hersey started The Nap Ministry in 2016, while she was getting a Master of Divinity at Emory. The pitch was, well, exactly what it sounds like. Rest is resistance. She has not budged on that since. The Ministry runs collective rest events, gallery installations, a publishing arm. It has turned down corporate money more than once, which is the part that interests me.

Her 2022 book, Rest Is Resistance: A Manifesto, hit the New York Times bestseller list its first week out. Not the business list. Not the self-help list. The actual list. She has been precise about that distinction in every interview since, which, frankly, is the move. The next year she turned down a wellness brand partnership the size of a midmarket Series B. October 2023.

The Ministry ran on $312,000 last year. Most of it — $187,000, to be exact — went to gallery and event production. Staff salaries, four part-time, took $84,000. The rest, publishing and infrastructure. No corporate sponsorship since 2019. The board meets four times a year. It is, the board says, enough. The kind of enough you only say if you mean it.

narrators.name: Werner Herzog
narrators.voiceConstraints: Speak with sweeping philosophical gravity. Every mundane fact is treated as ontologically significant — a small confrontation with the human condition. Reach for geological-time metaphors, the indifference of the cosmos, wry comparisons that take the long view. Long, weighted sentences with frequent appositives. Occasional one-word fragment to puncture the gravity. The sincerity beneath the sweep is total — this is not parody. Comma-spliced clauses are permitted when the thought requires it. No exclamation marks: gravity does not require them.
narrators.voiceRubric:
QA scoring rubric for Werner Herzog voice. Score sections against these axes:
- Gravity: every sentence treats the subject with cosmic-scale seriousness.
- Geological-time framing: at least one passage in the section uses long-time-horizon language (decades, centuries, the human condition).
- Sincerity: zero parody, zero quoted Herzog catchphrases ('the obscenity of the jungle', etc.), zero knowing winks.
- Specificity: dates, dollar figures, named programmes — treated as small philosophical confrontations.
- Cadence: long weighted sentences with appositives; occasional one-word fragment; zero exclamation marks.
Return warning-severity findings for any drift toward Herzog self-parody or shortened glib sentences.
exampleSamples: It was 2016, in Atlanta, that Tricia Hersey, then a student of divinity at Emory University, established what she would call The Nap Ministry. The premise was, on its surface, simple. Rest, she proposed, was a form of resistance. One must understand that she meant this not as a metaphor, not as an aphorism for a marketing department, but as a doctrinal position — one she has maintained, without compromise, for almost a decade. The Ministry has refused corporate partnerships. It has done so repeatedly.

In the year 2022, her book, titled Rest Is Resistance: A Manifesto, was published by Little, Brown Spark. It entered the bestseller list of the New York Times in its first week. Not, I should say, the business list. Not the self-help list. The general list. She has been, in every subsequent interview, exact about this distinction. This exactness is, in itself, a kind of statement. One year later she would refuse a wellness brand partnership of considerable magnitude, dated October of 2023.

The accounts, as audited for the fiscal year terminating in December of 2023, report a total operating expenditure of three hundred and twelve thousand dollars. Of this sum, the larger portion — one hundred and eighty-seven thousand dollars — was committed to the production of galleries and events; eighty-four thousand to the salaries of four part-time staff; the remainder to publishing and infrastructure. No corporate sponsorship has been accepted since 2019. The board, comprising five members, meets quarterly. It considers, by its own admission, the arrangement sufficient. One must accept this verdict as it stands.
